Definition: a (female) calf, especially one nearly grown (i.e. a heifer)
BiblicalUsage: A heifer is a young cow, and the Bible uses her in covenant, in atonement, and in daily work. God tells Abram to take a heifer three years old for the covenant, the law commands a heifer to be killed when a slain man is found in a field and no one knows who struck him, and Samuel takes a heifer to Bethlehem so his journey to anoint David looks like a sacrifice. Hosea pictures Israel as a trained heifer that loves to tread out the corn, working in comfort until the yoke comes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heifer shows how God meets His people in the ordinary work of the field, because He takes a farm animal and makes it part of His covenant and His law. The God of the threshing floor is the God of the promise too.
